item.title: SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository
item.description:
SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository

SafeLine has newly appeared as a top-ranked GitHub trending repository for Go projects, establishing itself as a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) designed to protect web applications from attacks and exploits.

🔍 Overview

SafeLine is a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect web apps from attacks and exploits. A web application firewall helps protect web apps by filtering and monitoring HTTP traffic between a web application and the Internet.

🧩 How it Works

Unlike a proxy server that protects a client machine’s identity, a WAF operates as a reverse-proxy, shielding the server by routing client requests through the firewall before reaching the server. A WAF protects web apps by filtering, monitoring, and blocking malicious HTTP/S traffic while preventing unauthorized data from leaving the application. This is achieved through policies that distinguish between malicious and safe traffic.

⚙️ Key Details

SafeLine’s core capabilities include:

Capability Description
Block Web Attacks Defends against SQL injection, XSS, code injection, os command injection, CRLF injection, XXE, SSRF, path traversal, and other web attacks
Rate Limiting Thwarts DoS attacks, bruteforce attempts, traffic surges, and abuse by throttling excessive traffic
Anti-Bot Challenge Blocks bots and crawlers while allowing human users through challenge mechanisms
Authentication Challenge Requires password entry for visitors when enabled, blocking unauthenticated access
Dynamic Protection Dynamically encrypts HTML and JavaScript code with each visit to the web server

Additional features include defenses for web attacks, proactive bot abuse defense, HTML & JS code encryption, IP-based rate limiting, and Web Access Control List.

🚀 Availability

SafeLine has achieved significant recognition on GitHub:

  • #1 GitHub Trending Repository
  • #1 Go Repository of the Day
  • #1 Go Repository of the Week
  • #9 Go Repository of the Month

💡 Why It Matters

The rise of SafeLine highlights growing community interest in self-hosted, open-source security solutions for web application protection, offering organizations an auditable alternative to commercial WAF offerings.

#WAF #cybersecurity #GoLang #GitHub #WebSecurity

Source: chaitin/SafeLine

item.title: Kronk Released as a Go SDK and Server for Local AI Inference
item.description:
Kronk Released as a Go SDK and Server for Local AI Inference

Kronk has been released as a Go SDK and production-ready model server designed for hardware-accelerated local inference. It allows developers to use Go to directly integrate llama.cpp, whisper.cpp, and stable-diffusion.cpp into their applications.

🔍 Overview

The Kronk model server is built on the same public SDKs that are available to Go applications. The system provides a high-level API and integrates with OpenWebUI, OpenCode, and Claude Code. It also includes features for model management, security, observability, and a browser interface.

⚙️ Key Components

The capabilities of Kronk are divided across several subsystems and SDK features:

Subsystem / Component Supported Capabilities and Features
Kronk SDK Text generation, streaming, reasoning, tool calls, vision, embeddings, reranking, typed Decision questions, buffered text-to-speech, concurrent processing, and incremental message caching.
Kronk Model Server OpenAI-compatible APIs (for Chat Completions, Responses, embeddings, reranking, and audio transcription), Anthropic-compatible Messages API, and Decision endpoints at /v1/systemone and /v1/decide.
Speech Supports Chatterbox Turbo and Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base with memory planning and typed pools across native backends. Currently SDK-only (no HTTP speech-generation endpoint or BUI speech playground).
Bucky File transcription, translation, channel-separated diarization, and live streaming transcription.
Experimental Malina Text-to-image, image-to-image, Canny ControlNet conditioning, ADetailer face refinement, AnimateDiff video generation, Real-ESRGAN upscaling, single-checkpoint and multi-file diffusion pipelines, and Motion-JPEG encoding. Currently SDK-only.

🧩 Hardware Acceleration and Dependencies

Kronk’s performance and execution model rely on several hardware and library management behaviors:

  • Automatic Downloads: The first model or SDK example that runs can download the compatible native libraries and model files automatically.
  • Library Management: Every Kronk release is bound to known-compatible library versions. Instead of mixing native libraries from unrelated releases, users should use each subsystem’s downloader. Upstream changes can require coordinated releases of Yzma, Bucky, Malina, and Kronk.
  • Acceleration Support: Hardware acceleration depends on the operating system, architecture, inference engine, and library bundle. Not every backend is available for every SDK or architecture, and non-Metal memory estimates are provisional.
  • Formula Trust: The fully qualified formula name trusts only the Kronk formula, rather than every item in the ardanlabs/kronk tap.

#Golang #Inference #LLM #DeveloperTools

Source: ardanlabs/kronk

item.title: NornicDB combines graph and vector search with sub-millisecond latency
item.description:
NornicDB combines graph and vector search with sub-millisecond latency

🔍 Overview

NornicDB is a distributed, low-latency database that integrates Graph and Vector capabilities with Temporal MVCC. It is designed to provide sub-millisecond performance for HNSW search, graph traversal, and writes.

🧩 How it works

The system allows users to query connected data using Cypher with compatible Bolt drivers. It supports combining graph traversal with vector and full-text retrieval. Historical state can be modeled using MVCC and retained history.

⚙️ Key details

  • Interfaces: Supports Neo4j Bolt/Cypher and qdrant’s gRPC, allowing switching without changes.
  • Features: Includes schemas, managed embeddings, reranking, LLM integration, GPU acceleration, Auto-TLP, Policy-based Memory Decay, and an MCP server.
  • Architecture: Multi-arch support includes CPU, CUDA, Metal, and Vulkan.
  • Integration: Can be embedded in Go applications and supports HTTP interfaces.

🚀 Availability

NornicDB is available via Docker images and native installers.

Platform Instructions
NVIDIA CUDA Use image timothyswt/nornicdb-amd64-cuda-bge:latest
Vulkan Use image timothyswt/nornicdb-amd64-vulkan-bge:latest
macOS Docker does not expose Metal acceleration; native install or local build required for GPU acceleration. Download .pkg installer (arm64 for Apple Silicon, amd64 for Intel) or use Homebrew.
Windows Run .\bin\nornicdb.exe serve

Users can access the admin UI at http://localhost:7474. Benchmark results depend on workload and hardware.

#GraphDatabase #VectorSearch #Cypher #NornicDB #GoLang

Source: orneryd/NornicDB

item.title: Update to Agent Development Kit with Go Toolkit Support
item.description:
Update to Agent Development Kit with Go Toolkit Support

The Agent Development Kit (ADK) has been updated with an open-source, code-first Go toolkit designed for building, evaluating, and deploying AI agents.

🔍 Overview

ADK is a modular framework that applies software development principles to the creation of AI agents. It simplifies the orchestration of agent workflows, ranging from simple tasks to complex systems. While optimized for Gemini, the framework is model-agnostic, deployment-agnostic, and compatible with other frameworks.

⚙️ Key details

The Go version of ADK leverages Go’s performance and concurrency strengths for cloud-native agent applications. Key features include:

  • Idiomatic Go: Designed to feel natural to Go developers.
  • Code-First Development: Agent logic, tools, and orchestration are defined directly in Go to provide flexibility, versioning, and testability.
  • Rich Tool Ecosystem: Supports custom functions, pre-built tools, or the integration of existing tools.
  • Modular Multi-Agent Systems: Allows for the composition of multiple specialized agents to create scalable applications.
  • Deploy Anywhere: Supports easy containerization and deployment, specifically for cloud-native environments such as Google Cloud Run.

🚀 Availability

Developers can add ADK Go to a project using the following command: go get google.golang.org/adk/v2

Machine-readable documentation is available at adk.dev/llms.txt and adk.dev/llms-full.txt, both of which are generated from the adk-docs repository and include samples and the Go API reference.

🧩 Ecosystem Support

ADK is available across several languages and platforms:

Language/Platform Link
Python https://github.com/google/adk-python
Java https://github.com/google/adk-java
Kotlin https://github.com/google/adk-kotlin
TypeScript https://github.com/google/adk-js
Web https://github.com/google/adk-web

This project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License, with the exception of internal/httprr.

#GoLang #AIAgents #OpenSource #CloudNative

Source: google/adk-go

item.title: Go Micro Released as Agent Harness and Service Framework for Go
item.description:
Go Micro Released as Agent Harness and Service Framework for Go

Go Micro has been introduced as an agent harness and service framework for the Go programming language. It provides a runtime environment that treats agents as distributed systems, allowing developers to build agents and services within a single runtime.

🔍 Overview

A harness in this context refers to the runtime around an agent, including its tools, memory, guardrails, triggering workflows, dependent services, and the protocols used by other agents to reach it. Go Micro provides this harness as Go code.

🧩 How it works

Go Micro allows for the description of a system, which it then uses to design services, write handlers, compile them, and start them. Key capabilities include:

  • Agent Components: Agents are equipped with a model, memory, tools, planning, delegation, guardrails, and service discovery.
  • Connectivity: Agents are reachable via MCP and A2A.
  • Tooling: Every endpoint in a written service becomes an AI-callable tool.
  • Orchestration: Durable flows are used to orchestrate deterministic parts of the system.
  • Dynamic Development: If an agent requires a capability that does not exist, it can build the service mid-conversation.
  • Code Management: Generated code is plain Go on disk, which can be edited by hand; re-running the process preserves these changes.

⚙️ Key details

Go Micro includes a CLI and specialized commands for agent management and debugging:

Command Function
micro chat Talk to the agent
micro agent demo Prints the provider-free first-agent walkthrough
micro agent quickcheck Prints a short recovery map if a step stalls
micro agent preflight Run before micro run
micro agent doctor Run after micro run
micro inspect agent <name> Recovers run history, memory, and provider checks
micro examples Prints runnable examples
micro zero-to-hero Prints the one-command lifecycle harness

🚀 Availability

Users can install the CLI via the following methods:

  • Shell script: curl -fsSL https://go-micro.dev/install.sh | sh
  • Go install: go install go-micro.dev/v6/cmd/micro@latest
  • Docker: Available via Docker Hub (micro/micro) or GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io/micro/go-micro).

To scaffold and run a service, the following workflow is used:

  1. micro new helloworld
  2. cd helloworld
  3. micro run

#GoLang #AIagents #SoftwareDevelopment #DistributedSystems

Source: micro/go-micro
